questions.question: How do you work with JSON and YAML in Ruby?
questions.title: JSON and YAML in Ruby
questions.direct_answer: JSON and YAML are serialization formats — they turn Ruby objects into text and back. JSON (require 'json'): JSON.dump(obj) -> a JSON string; JSON.parse(str) -> a Hash/Array (string keys!); JSON.parse(str, symbolize_names: true) -> symbol keys. YAML (require 'yaml'): YAML.dump(obj) -> YAML text; YAML.load(str) (or safe_load) -> Ruby objects. JSON is the wire format for APIs (compact, universal); YAML is common for config (Gemfile, database.yml) because it's human-readable and supports comments. The catch: JSON.parse gives string keys by default (use symbolize_names: true); YAML.load can execute arbitrary objects, so use YAML.safe_load in production. Use JSON for API payloads, YAML for config files.

interviewer_intent.testing: Whether you know JSON.parse/JSON.dump (and symbolize_names) and YAML.load/safe_load, and when to use each (JSON APIs, YAML config).
interviewer_intent.common_mistake: JSON.parse giving string keys (use symbolize_names: true), or YAML.load (unsafe) instead of safe_load in production.
interviewer_intent.to_stand_out: JSON (require 'json'): JSON.dump/parse (symbolize_names: true for symbol keys). YAML (require 'yaml'): dump/load/safe_load. JSON for APIs, YAML for config; safe_load in prod.

sections.title: Serialize to Text and Back
sections.content: JSON and YAML are serialization formats — they turn Ruby objects into text and back. JSON (require json): JSON dot dump obj to a JSON string; JSON dot parse str to a Hash or Array (string keys); JSON dot parse str symbolize_names true to symbol keys. YAML (require yaml): YAML dot dump obj to YAML text; YAML dot load str (or safe_load) to Ruby objects. JSON is the wire format for APIs (compact, universal); YAML is common for config (Gemfile, database dot yml) because it's human-readable and supports comments. The catch: JSON dot parse gives string keys by default (use symbolize_names true); YAML dot load can execute arbitrary objects, so use YAML dot safe_load in production. Use JSON for API payloads, YAML for config files.

sections.title: JSON vs YAML
sections.content:
JSON.dump/parse (symbolize_names for :keys); YAML.dump/load/safe_load. JSON for APIs, YAML for config.

```mermaid
flowchart LR
  J[JSON: require 'json'] --> Dp[JSON.dump -> String]
  Dp --> Ps[JSON.parse -> Hash; symbolize_names: true]
  Y[YAML: require 'yaml'] --> Yd[YAML.dump -> text]
  Yd --> Yl[YAML.load / safe_load]
```

sections.title: JSON and YAML
sections.content:
```ruby
require 'json'
require 'yaml'

# JSON: Ruby <-> text
json_str = JSON.dump({ name: 'Ada', age: 30 })   # '{"name":"Ada","age":30}'
obj = JSON.parse(json_str)            # {"name"=>"Ada","age"=>30} (STRING keys)
obj = JSON.parse(json_str, symbolize_names: true)  # {name:'Ada', age:30} (:keys)

# JSON.generate / JSON.parse are the core pair.
# In Rails, render json: @post and parse params automatically.

# YAML: Ruby <-> text (human-readable; used for config)
yaml_str = YAML.dump({ name: 'Ada', age: 30 })
#   ---
#   :name: Ada
#   :age: 30
obj = YAML.safe_load(yaml_str)        # safe_load (not load) in production

# Read a config file:
config = YAML.safe_load(File.read('database.yml'))

# Use JSON for API payloads (compact, universal). YAML for config (readable, comments).
# CAUTION: YAML.load can deserialize arbitrary objects -> use safe_load in prod.
```

sections.title: Common Mistakes
items: JSON.parse giving string keys (use symbolize_names: true).
Using YAML.load (unsafe) instead of safe_load in production.
Picking YAML for an API payload (JSON is compact and universal).

sections.title: Key Takeaways
items: JSON.parse gives string keys by default — use symbolize_names: true for :keys.
YAML (require 'yaml'): YAML.dump -> text; YAML.load / safe_load -> Ruby objects.
JSON is the wire format for APIs (compact, universal); YAML is for config (readable, comments).
Use YAML.safe_load (not load) in production — load can deserialize arbitrary objects.
